chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb al-Hāshimī, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The salat (prayer) is not missed for one who intends the salat (prayer): the daytime salat (prayer) is not missed until the sun sets, nor the nighttime salat (prayer) until dawn rises, nor the fajr salat (prayer) until the sun rises.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer); the prescribed ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ: the sun rises; the endpoint for fajr salat (prayer) time mentioned here
key_terms.تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ: the sun sets; the endpoint for daytime prayer time mentioned here
key_terms.صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ: the nighttime salat (prayer), referring contextually to prayers whose time extends through the night
key_terms.صَلَاةُ النَّهَارِ: the daytime salat (prayer), referring contextually to prayers performed before sunset
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْفَجْرِ: the fajr salat (prayer), the dawn prayer
key_terms.يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ: dawn rises; the endpoint for nighttime prayer time mentioned here

ai.seo_question: Until what time is a prayer considered valid and not yet missed in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the outer limits of prayer times, indicating that a prayer is not considered missed so long as its remaining valid time has not fully ended. It addresses daytime prayers, nighttime prayers, and fajr salat (prayer), clarifying their final time boundaries in a legal context.
